analysis: Examined the modified test-only file provider-swift/Tests/ClusterPlacementChecks/PlacementSetupCheck.swift (head lines 1-630 supplied). The only changed range in the patch (head ~1260-1264, outside the supplied excerpt) updates a require() check to pass a new `publicModels: []` argument to ClusterPairServingGrants.publicTrafficLine. This is a test-only edit and changes no production code, network, key-handling, attestation or cache path. The supplied lines are check fixtures. They use synthetic hashes, 192.0.2.x documentation IPs and fixture paths, and contain no secrets. They exercise developer-only toggles (DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_FORCE_MODE, DARKBLOOM_DEV_BENCH_*, hand-off opt-in) and assert that a release build refuses them. That is consistent with fail-closed behavior, not a regression. None of the supplied content touches TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, T-041 or the prefix-cache storage. The test file does not weaken any threat-model mitigation. Remaining integration question: the production signature change of publicTrafficLine (new publicModels parameter, presumably a public-declaration gate for traffic qualification) lies in files outside this batch. Whether it correctly fails closed when the public declaration is absent was not visible here. The test asserts that with publicModels: [] a family that has a passing record still reports 'qualified for public traffic' for phaseSplit, which is worth verifying against the production implementation. I saw no evidence of a defect.
